questions.explanation: Abundant means existing in large quantities, which is the same as plentiful.
questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to ABUNDANT.

questions.explanation: Generous means willing to give freely, so its opposite is stingy, meaning unwilling to give.
questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to GENEROUS.

questions.explanation: The verb insisted is followed by the preposition on when it takes a gerund, as in insisted on submitting.
questions.q: Fill in the blank: The manager insisted ___ submitting the report before noon.

questions.explanation: With neither/nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject; the plural subject students requires were listening, not was listening.
questions.q: Identify the part with an error: Neither the teacher (A) nor the students (B) was listening (C) attentively. No error (D)

questions.explanation: To burn the midnight oil means to work or study late into the night.
options: To study or work late at night
questions.q: What does the idiom TO BURN THE MIDNIGHT OIL mean?

questions.explanation: Candid means honest and straightforward, so its opposite is deceptive.
questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to CANDID.

questions.explanation: Neither of takes a singular verb, so the correct choice is is qualified.
questions.q: Fill in the blank: Neither of the candidates ___ qualified for the post.

questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail, which is the same as thorough.
questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to METICULOUS.

questions.explanation: A blessing in disguise is something that seems bad at first but turns out to be beneficial.
questions.q: What does the idiom A BLESSING IN DISGUISE mean?

questions.explanation: The adjective senior is followed by the preposition to, not than.
questions.q: Fill in the blank: She is senior ___ me by two years.
